newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-French, German stocks slide; London flat.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French, German stocks slide; London flat.

text.p: French and German stocks fell sharply in early trade on Friday, weighed down by a poor overnight close on Wall Street, a weaker dollar and a sudden bout of political jitters.
The Paris bourse was worst hit, dropping 2.25 percent on worries over a snap election. Frankfurt lost over one percent as the falling dollar dimmed export prospects and London made a flat start.
The U.S. currency slipped against the mark after the German central bank chief President Hans Tietmeyer's comment on Thursday that the Bundesbank was not interested in seeing the mark weaken further.

The big fall in the French CAC 40 index came after President Jacques Chirac failed to calm rumours on Thursday about a snap election or cabinet reshuffle, and the opposition Socialist party said it was ready to contest a vote.
"Political uncertainties and a lower dollar are driving the market down," one trader said, although he added that the volume of early transactions was thin.

Amid political shadow-boxing, the Socialists accused Chirac of considering parliamentary elections a year early to renew the centre-right majority before a new bout of austerity to help France qualify for a single European currency.

Government spokesman Alain Lamassoure denied speculation that Chirac might justify an election by arguing that greater fiscal rigour was needed. "We have no budgetary problems at the moment," he said.
In Frankfurt, stocks were also well down, partially catching up with losses in after-hours electronic trade last night, but also because of the dollar and New York's negative close.
Dealers said the market lacked clear direction going into the weekend. "We haven't had any real orders," said a trader at a large Frankfurt bank. "Things are just creaking along."

London, Europe's biggest bourse, made the best start, slipping only slightly. But the market's mood was lethargic as pre-election nerves and fears of rising interest rates put a lid on active trading.
"We've totally decoupled from the Dow," one trader said as the FTSE index was barely changed from Thursday's closing level of 4,298.9 points."We seem to be stuck around the 4,300 level."
The Dow broke its three-day winning streak on Thursday to finish 21.27 points or 0.32 percent lower at 6,658.60, after jumping 288 points in the previous three sessions.

Trading volumes have shrunk recently as investors have become increasingly shy of the market so close to the election on May 1. Analysts are also factoring in an interest rate rise of between 25 and 50 basis points soon after the election which is further dampening sentiment.
Shares in British Telecommunications Plc firmed 6-1/2p to 449p in active trade, after news of a global alliance with its merger partner MCI Communications and Telefonica de Espana.
On currency markets, the dollar lost nearly a pfennig in early trade, because of Teitmeyer's remarks, before recovering slightly though it was virtually unchaged against the yen.
"The Germans have given up their long-standing silence on exchange rates...and that's made a pretty significant impact on the market," DMG's Baader said.

"It's a lot less aggressive position than that of the Japanese... But the German position had been perceived as gladly accepting any depreciation of the mark, so in that sense it was an important statement, although it wasn't as strong as it might have been," Baader said.

Against the yen, the dollar started the day weaker before perking up. It had been hit by remarks made overnight by Eisuke Sakakibara, the influential head of the Japanese Finance Ministry's international finance bureau.

Sakakibara, in an interview with Reuters, warned of the danger of assuming Japan would not raise interest rates within the next year, saying it would be natural for the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates when the strength of the economy was confirmed.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7168 marks and 125.87 yen after ending at 1.7241 and 125.97 in late trading in Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 1.3 points at 4,297.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 54.28 points at 2,560.85
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 33.19 points at 3,350.06.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in London at $342.00 versus $343.15 at the close in London on Thursday. Silver was three cents lower at $4.73.
